offers.title: Three ways to start
offers.intro: Pick the one that sounds like your week. Each one starts with the free audit.

items.name: Product development
items.situation: You have an idea or a spec, and no team yet.
items.text: We cut the first release down to what proves the idea, then design it, build it and launch it. When your own hires arrive, we hand the code over.
items.get: Working software every Friday, from the first week of the build.
items.who: Founders and product owners at startups, scale-ups and manufacturers.

items.name: Stabilise and scale
items.situation: Your product is live, but releases break, the team is slow or the original developers left.
items.text: We take over where your last team stopped, stabilise the product and get it moving again.
items.get: A before and after report on deploys, failed releases and build time.

items.name: Team augmentation
items.situation: Your team needs senior hands now, and hiring takes months.
items.text: Our engineers join your standups, your tickets and your code review. Each month you decide whether to scale up or down.
items.get: A first merged pull request in the first week.

items.name: Product design, part time
items.text: A designer two days a week: user flows, a small design system and usability checks.

items.name: AI engineering setup for your team
items.text: We bring AI coding tools into your team with rules attached: which repositories, which models, what a reviewer checks and how to measure the effect.

expertise.title: Stacks we've shipped. Yours is probably close.
expertise.intro: A senior engineer picks up a neighbouring stack in days, and the review bar stays the same.

route.title: Three routes, one per offer
route.intro: Every route starts with the free audit, runs through Build and ends with a handover to your own team. Click a line to ride it, or a station to look inside.

items.q: Do you use AI to write code?
items.a: We use AI tools where they save you time. A senior engineer reviews every change.
Two weeks from a signed contract to the first commit.
You do. The code lives in your repository, and we hand over documentation when your own hires take over.

items.q: Which time zone do you work in?
items.a: Central European Time, the same as Berlin, Vienna and Zurich. Our office is in Cluj-Napoca, Romania.

items.q: What does the free audit cover?
items.a: Five working days on two areas you pick, then a written report and a walkthrough with your team.

how.title: A small senior team
how.intro: We staff one or two developers, with design and DevOps alongside. You get the same people every week, and they hand over clean code when your own hires arrive.
